incidents.cause: The pilot's inadequate flare during landing.  Contributing to the accident was the uneven terrain.
The pilot/builder's misjudgment of the required spacer width needed after engine housing lap grinding, which resulted in bearing oil hole misalignment and insufficient internal engine lubrication.
A partial loss of engine power due to the formation of carburetor ice while on the ground, which resulted in reduced climb capability and impact with trees during the initial climb.
The pilot's inadequate fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
Fatigue failure of the left main wheel assembly on takeoff, which resulted in a loss of directional control and runway excursion.
The pilot's improper recovery from a bounced landing, which resulted in a loss of control.
Improper maintenance practices on the fuel system causing fuel starvation and a total loss of engine power.
The pilot misjudged the landing approach, which resulted in the airplane hitting a tree.
